summary.summary: Brent's 2024/25 outturn shows external borrowing up £85.8m (10.5%) to £900.0m, funding a capital programme that pushed the Loan CFR up £102.6m to £1,357.1m (General Fund £1,015.1m, HRA £342.0m). A £13.7m budget variance on capital financing costs (£41.5m actual against a £27.8m budget) was offset by a drawdown from capital reserves. The council has grown related-party lending to its wholly-owned housing companies — £182.4m to I4B Holdings Ltd and £33.8m to First Wave Housing — and holds £59.5m of LOBO loans, of which £35.0m face an interest-rate review in 2025/26.

signals.headline: External borrowing rose £85.8m (10.5%) to £900.0m in 2024/25, from £170.0m of new loans against £84.2m of repayments.
signals.why: A rapid, double-digit rise in the debt stock within a single year.

signals.headline: A £13.7m capital-financing budget variance (£41.5m actual vs £27.8m budget) was offset by drawing down capital reserves.
signals.why: Financing costs are already outrunning budget, absorbed by reserves rather than a revised budget.

signals.headline: £35.0m of the council's £59.5m LOBO book (5 loans) is due an interest-rate review in 2025/26.
signals.why: If a lender exercises its option the council's own option is to repay at par, which is what councils do: every LOBO call we hold — Kent, Tameside, Newcastle, York, Barnet, Brighton and Hove, Bristol — was repaid rather than accepted. So the exposure is finding £35.0m and replacing that funding at today's rates, not paying a higher rate on it.

signals.headline: Loans to Brent's wholly-owned companies stood at £182.4m to I4B Holdings Ltd and £33.8m to First Wave Housing at 31 March 2025, both secured on company property, plus a £36.4m equity stake in I4B.
signals.why: Sizeable related-party credit exposure sits alongside the headline treasury debt figures.

findings.paper_title: 10g. Appendix G - LB Brent Auditor's Annual Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Dedicated Schools Grant cumulative deficit rose to £20.2m but High Needs Stability Grant will fund 90% of deficit
findings.detail: The cumulative DSG deficit at end of 2025-26 rose to £20.2m, reflecting ongoing SEND service pressures. Prior to recent government announcements, the council would have needed to meet this from revenue reserves by end of 2027-28. The council is now eligible for the High Needs Stability Grant, supporting up to 90% of deficits at end of 2025-26. Management used a £2.1m increase in Revenue Support Grant (from technical baseline change) to create a new reserve covering the remaining 10%.
findings.matters: While SEND pressures remain significant, the government's High Needs Stability Grant removes immediate risk that the council would need to meet this deficit from revenue reserves, materially mitigating what would otherwise be severe medium-term financial pressure.
findings.figures: £20.2m cumulative DSG deficit; High Needs Stability Grant covers 90% of deficits; £2.1m RSG increase allocated to cover remaining 10%
findings.quote: The cumulative DSG deficit at the end of 2025-26 rose to £20.2m. Prior to recent government announcements the Council needed to meet deficits from its revenue reserves at the end of 2027-28. Now, the Council is eligible for government support, in the form of the High Needs Stability Grant, supporting up to 90% of deficits at the end of 2025-26.

findings.paper_title: 10g. Appendix G - LB Brent Auditor's Annual Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Council moved to no overall control (NOC) status in May 2026, first time in over a decade, introducing governance complexity
findings.detail: Following the 7 May 2026 local elections, the Labour group won 26 of 57 seats but failed to secure overall majority, resulting in no overall control status for the first time in over a decade. Councillor Muhammed Butt leads a Labour minority administration. The auditor notes that with new Members and changed political balance, 'governance arrangements are being reviewed and updated' and specifically flags need to 'stress-test constitutional provisions for budget amendments, given the more complex path to agreement under NOC.'
findings.matters: No overall control typically slows decision-making, requires cross-party negotiation, and creates uncertainty around policy continuity. For a council facing significant financial pressures and needing to deliver substantial savings, this introduces governance risk.
findings.figures: 26 Labour seats out of 57 total (no overall majority); first NOC status in over a decade
findings.quote: Following the local elections held on 7 May 2026, Labour remained the largest political group with 26 seats, but no party secured an overall majority, resulting in a council under no overall control (NOC). Councillor Muhammed Butt continues as Leader of the Council, leading a Labour minority administration

findings.paper_title: 10g. Appendix G - LB Brent Auditor's Annual Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Pension Fund improved significantly to 113% funded at March 2025, up from 87% at prior valuation
findings.detail: The Brent Pension Fund's most recent formal valuation (31 March 2025) assessed it as 113% funded, representing substantial improvement from 87% funded at the March 2022 valuation. The Fund is estimated to be able to meet pension liabilities with available assets. Fund management costs are comparatively low at 0.179% of net investment assets. The fund must transition all investment assets to the London Collective Investment Vehicle (LCIV) pooling arrangement by 30 September 2026 under new regulations; 93% of assets were already pooled as at 31 March 2026.
findings.matters: A well-funded pension fund reduces the council's long-term liability and capital requirements, improving the council's overall financial position. However, the pooling transition must be managed successfully to avoid operational disruption.
findings.figures: Pension Fund 113% funded at March 2025 (up from 87% at March 2022); management costs 0.179% of net assets; 93% of assets pooled as at 31 March 2026; Sept 2026 deadline
findings.quote: The most recent formal valuation, as at 31 March 2025, assessed the whole Pension Fund as being 113% funded. This is a strong position whereby the Fund is estimated to be able to meet its pension liabilities with its available assets. This is a significant and positive improvement from 87% funded at last valuation (March 2022).

findings.paper_title: 10g. Appendix G - LB Brent Auditor's Annual Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Regulator of Social Housing maintained C3 rating with fire, water and asbestos safety compliance still significantly below standard
findings.detail: The Regulator of Social Housing (RSH) issued a C3 'requires improvement' rating in May 2025 following the council's self-referral for failing to meet the Safety and Quality Standard on fire safety and housing repairs. Over 2025-26, the council implemented a Housing and Tenant Satisfaction Improvement Programme. However, as of June 2026, compliance remains poor: fire safety risk assessments at 69%, legionella and water safety at 71%, and asbestos reinspection at only 5%. Additionally, 1,700 housing assets (19% of stock) still have no stock condition survey on record. The council is targeting upgrade to C1 by 2029.
findings.matters: Regulatory intervention signals control failures in a significant service area. These compliance gaps present reputational and legal/financial risk for safety breaches, indicating governance gaps and a service requiring sustained financial investment.
findings.figures: Fire safety 69% compliant; legionella and water safety 71% compliant; asbestos reinspection 5% compliant; 1,700 assets (19% of stock) without surveys; C1 readiness target 2029
findings.quote: Following the Council's self-referral, the Regulator of Social Housing (RSH) gave a 'requires improvement' C3 rating for failing to meet the Safety and Quality Standard in relation to accuracy and completion of fire safety data and housing repairs.

findings.paper_title: 10g. Appendix G - LB Brent Auditor's Annual Report 2025-26
findings.headline: Council holds £53m more in current liabilities than current assets, creating working capital pressure
findings.detail: The council's balance sheet shows current assets are £53m below current liabilities, creating pressure should all liabilities fall due at once. The auditor raised Improvement Recommendation 2 on this issue, noting management should explore ways to strengthen the balance sheet through treasury management practices. Cash and short-term investments (22% of current assets) have reduced by 5% compared to prior year.
findings.matters: A negative working capital position means the council's liquid resources are insufficient to cover near-term obligations if they matured simultaneously. While local authorities manage this through borrowing facilities, it is a monitoring point for lenders assessing day-to-day liquidity.
findings.figures: £53m deficit of current assets against current liabilities; cash and short-term investments reduced by 5% year-on-year
findings.quote: Within this, the Council holds fewer current assets than current liabilities, creating pressure should all liabilities fall due at the same time. As such we raise Improvement Recommendation 2 to encourage management to consider how it can strengthen this position.
